existing_atlas_baseline.partner_json_observation: Fallback DiDi proposal is LatAm-led; _map_scope includes hong-kong-macau and cluster_city_ids hong-kong/macau-china. It does not yet include the Japan or Taiwan city IDs in its shown map scope.
existing_atlas_baseline.cluster_route_observation: Fallback route-stamp ledger records Japan cluster with 8 supplied city IDs and 161 stamped routes, Hong Kong–Macau with 2 cities and 54 stamped routes, and Taiwan with 2 cities and 7 stamped routes. It does not expose route IDs/endpoints, so no exact ROUTES.json ID matches were claimed.
existing_atlas_baseline.boarding_point_files: Matching atlas-external boarding-point files could not be inspected because the requested repo snapshot was absent.

sources.title: DiDi user service areas
sources.proves: Current official service-area roster names Niseko/Kutchan; Tokyo; Shizuoka including Atami and Ito; Hiroshima/Hatsukaichi and other Setouchi cities; Naha/main-island municipalities; Miyakojima; and Ishigaki. It warns that some remote islands are excluded.

sources.title: DiDi and SoftBank Launch Joint Venture in Japan to Offer Taxi-Hailing Services
sources.proves: Establishes DiDi Mobility Japan as the DiDi–SoftBank joint venture and says the service is taxi-hailing in Japan. It does not prove present Taiwan or Hong Kong local ride supply.

sources.title: DiDi and SoftBank Establish Joint Venture in Japan
sources.proves: Independent first-party JV framing for Japan.

sources.title: DiDi Japan Launches Taxi-Hailing Service in Hokkaido
sources.proves: Historical launch receipt for Hokkaido; current exact coverage is instead taken from the live DiDi Mobility Japan roster.

sources.title: DiDi China: Ride Hailing — Hong Kong App Store listing
sources.proves: A current Hong Kong storefront listing and recent developer activity prove app availability, not by themselves a current Hong Kong city service-area roster.

sources.title: How many countries does DiDi operate in?
sources.proves: Official country list surfaced in search did not name Taiwan; absence is not treated as definitive cessation evidence, but no current official Taiwan operation receipt was found.

sources.title: Information on Kurihama Port and Kanaya Port
sources.proves: Current ferry connects Kurihama Port and Kanaya Port across Tokyo Bay in about 40 minutes.

sources.title: Price list
sources.proves: Current page gives adult one-way passenger fare of JPY 1,100 and round trip JPY 2,000; page notes cash-only ticket sales.

sources.title: Timetable and Fares
sources.proves: Current official timetable/fare hub for Izu Islands; service dates June 1–September 30, 2026.

sources.title: High-speed jet ferry / large passenger ship timetable, July–September 2026
sources.proves: Current schedule proves Tokyo–Oshima and onward Izu-island service, Atami–Oshima service, Shimoda services, and service-day/seasonality patterns. Fare values were not extracted from this timetable.

sources.title: Vessel fare table
sources.proves: Official current terminal distinction and fares: Ferry Zamami uses Tomari south bank; Queen Zamami uses north bank. Naha–Zamami/Aka adult one-way is JPY 2,900 by ferry and JPY 3,950 by high-speed boat; JPY 100 island tax applies.

sources.title: Zamami Village passenger seating availability
sources.proves: Current live booking/availability page proves operating sailings and shows vessel, departure time and Aka stop where applicable.

sources.title: Ferries between islands
sources.proves: Official tourism guide identifies Tomarin/Tomari Wharf Passenger Terminal and Zamami travel times of roughly 50–70 minutes by express ferry or two hours by regular ferry.

sources.title: Welcome to Yaeyama Kanko Ferry
sources.proves: Current operator page exposes timetable, operation status, tickets, access and route map for Ishigaki/Yaeyama ferry services. Exact coordinates and current fare values require follow-up.

sources.title: Fare
sources.proves: Official one-way adult fare is JPY 180; a separate JPY 100 Miyajima visitor tax applies on entry.

sources.title: Miyajima Visitor Tax
sources.proves: Official tax page confirms JPY 100 per person per visit, generally collected by passenger-boat operators.

sources.title: Franchised and Licensed Ferry Service Details
sources.proves: Official route/terminal/schedule/fare evidence. North Point (West) Ferry Pier–Hung Hom (North) Ferry Pier is about 8 minutes, daily, HKD 10 adult one-way at the cited effective date.

sources.title: Ferries
sources.proves: Official system overview states 10 operators and 21 regular licensed passenger ferry services as of the page reference date.

sources.title: HKIA Serves 61 Million Passengers in 2025
sources.proves: HKIA handled 61 million passengers in calendar 2025; this is an airport catchment indicator, not ferry-route demand.

sources.title: HKTB announces 2025 full-year visitor arrivals
sources.proves: Hong Kong received about 49.9 million visitors in 2025; this broad visitor count must not be converted directly into route demand.

sources.title: Overview of the Environment in Okinawa Prefecture
sources.proves: Reports 9,668,800 visitors to Okinawa in 2024; catchment context only.

sources.title: Penghu Ferry booking system
sources.proves: Current operator booking surface for Kaohsiung–Penghu, including orders, vehicle shipping, fares and passenger guide.

sources.title: Kaohsiung ↔ Penghu timetable
sources.proves: Current 115-year (2026) sailing calendar proves the route is active but weather-disruption prone.

sources.title: Penghu Ferry fare information
sources.proves: Official fare page exists, but values are embedded in images and were not safely extracted; fare remains null.

sources.title: Japan tourism statistics data list
sources.proves: Official national visitor-arrivals series. National totals are not route demand and are not used as such.

Keep the vessel network and terminal facts partner-neutral in canonical briefs; put app-dispatch and first/last-mile language only in the DiDi sub-proposal.
